5011// Specifies how to handle stepped tangents.
5012typedef enum ufbx_bake_step_handling UFBX_ENUM_REPR {
5013
5014 // One millisecond default step duration, with potential extra slack for converting to `float`.
5015 UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING_DEFAULT,
5016
5017 // Use a custom interpolation duration for the constant step.
5018 // See `ufbx_bake_opts.step_custom_duration` and optionally `ufbx_bake_opts.step_custom_epsilon`.
5019 UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING_CUSTOM_DURATION,
5020
5021 // Stepped keyframes are represented as keyframes at the exact same time.
5022 // Use flags `UFBX_BAKED_KEY_STEP_LEFT` and `UFBX_BAKED_KEY_STEP_RIGHT` to differentiate
5023 // between the primary key and edge limits.
5024 UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING_IDENTICAL_TIME,
5025
5026 // Represent stepped keyframe times as the previous/next representable `double` value.
5027 // Using this and robust linear interpolation will handle stepped tangents correctly
5028 // without having to look at the key flags.
5029 // NOTE: Casting these values to `float` or otherwise modifying them can collapse
5030 // the keyframes to have the identical time.
5031 UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING_ADJACENT_DOUBLE,
5032
5033 // Treat all stepped tangents as linearly interpolated.
5034 UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING_IGNORE,
5035
5036 UFBX_ENUM_FORCE_WIDTH(ufbx_bake_step_handling)
5037} ufbx_bake_step_handling;
5038
5039UFBX_ENUM_TYPE(ufbx_bake_step_handling, UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING, UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING_IGNORE);
5040
5041typedef struct ufbx_bake_opts {
5042 uint32_t _begin_zero;
5043
5044 ufbx_allocator_opts temp_allocator; // < Allocator used during loading
5045 ufbx_allocator_opts result_allocator; // < Allocator used for the final baked animation
5046
5047 // Move the keyframe times to start from zero regardless of the animation start time.
5048 // For example, for an animation spanning between frames [30, 60] will be moved to
5049 // [0, 30] in the baked animation.
5050 // NOTE: This is in general not equivalent to subtracting `ufbx_anim.time_begin`
5051 // from each keyframe, as this trimming is done exactly using internal FBX ticks.
5052 bool trim_start_time;
5053
5054 // Samples per second to use for resampling non-linear animation.
5055 // Default: 30
5056 double resample_rate;
5057
5058 // Minimum sample rate to not resample.
5059 // Many exporters resample animation by default. To avoid double-resampling
5060 // keyframe rates higher or equal to this will not be resampled.
5061 // Default: 19.5
5062 double minimum_sample_rate;
5063
5064 // Maximum sample rate to use, this will remove keys if they are too close together.
5065 // Default: unlimited
5066 double maximum_sample_rate;
5067
5068 // Bake the raw versions of properties related to transforms.
5069 bool bake_transform_props;
5070
5071 // Do not bake node transforms.
5072 bool skip_node_transforms;
5073
5074 // Do not resample linear rotation keyframes.
5075 // FBX interpolates rotation in Euler angles, so this might cause incorrect interpolation.
5076 bool no_resample_rotation;
5077
5078 // Ignore layer weight animation.
5079 bool ignore_layer_weight_animation;
5080
5081 // Maximum number of segments to generate from one keyframe.
5082 // Default: 32
5083 size_t max_keyframe_segments;
5084
5085 // How to handle stepped tangents.
5086 ufbx_bake_step_handling step_handling;
5087
5088 // Interpolation duration used by `UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING_CUSTOM_DURATION`.
5089 double step_custom_duration;
5090
5091 // Interpolation epsilon used by `UFBX_BAKE_STEP_HANDLING_CUSTOM_DURATION`.
5092 // Defined as the minimum fractional decrease/increase in key time, ie.
5093 // `time / (1.0 + step_custom_epsilon)` and `time * (1.0 + step_custom_epsilon)`.
5094 double step_custom_epsilon;
5095
5096 // Flags passed to animation evaluation functions.
5097 // See `ufbx_evaluate_flags`.
5098 uint32_t evaluate_flags;
5099
5100 // Enable key reduction.
5101 bool key_reduction_enabled;
5102
5103 // Enable key reduction for non-constant rotations.
5104 // Assumes rotations will be interpolated using a spherical linear interpolation at runtime.
5105 bool key_reduction_rotation;
5106
5107 // Threshold for reducing keys for linear segments.
5108 // Default `0.000001`, use negative to disable.
5109 double key_reduction_threshold;
5110
5111 // Maximum passes over the keys to reduce.
5112 // Every pass can potentially halve the the amount of keys.
5113 // Default: `4`
5114 size_t key_reduction_passes;
5115
5116 uint32_t _end_zero;
5117} ufbx_bake_opts;

5449
5450// Flags to control `ufbx_evaluate_transform_flags()`.
5451typedef enum ufbx_transform_flags UFBX_FLAG_REPR {
5452
5453 // Ignore parent scale helper.
5454 UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_IGNORE_SCALE_HELPER = 0x1,
5455
5456 // Ignore componentwise scale.
5457 // Note that if you don't specify this, ufbx will have to potentially
5458 // evaluate the entire parent chain in the worst case.
5459 UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_IGNORE_COMPONENTWISE_SCALE = 0x2,
5460
5461 // Require explicit components
5462 UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_EXPLICIT_INCLUDES = 0x4,
5463
5464 // If `UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_EXPLICIT_INCLUDES`: Evaluate `ufbx_transform.translation`.
5465 UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_INCLUDE_TRANSLATION = 0x10,
5466 // If `UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_EXPLICIT_INCLUDES`: Evaluate `ufbx_transform.rotation`.
5467 UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_INCLUDE_ROTATION = 0x20,
5468 // If `UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_EXPLICIT_INCLUDES`: Evaluate `ufbx_transform.scale`.
5469 UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_INCLUDE_SCALE = 0x40,
5470
5471 // Do not extrapolate keyframes.
5472 // See `UFBX_EVALUATE_FLAG_NO_EXTRAPOLATION`.
5473 UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAG_NO_EXTRAPOLATION = 0x80,
5474
5475 UFBX_FLAG_FORCE_WIDTH(UFBX_TRANSFORM_FLAGS)
5476} ufbx_transform_flags;

5917// RAII wrapper over refcounted ufbx types.
5918
5919// Behaves like `std::unique_ptr<T>`.
5920template <typename T>
5921class ufbx_unique_ptr {
5922 T *ptr;
5923 using traits = ufbx_type_traits<T>;
5924 static_assert(ufbx_type_traits<T>::valid, "ufbx_unique_ptr unsupported for type");
5925public:
5926 ufbx_unique_ptr() noexcept : ptr(nullptr) { }
5927 explicit ufbx_unique_ptr(T *ptr_) noexcept : ptr(ptr_) { }
5928 ufbx_unique_ptr(ufbx_unique_ptr &&ref) noexcept : ptr(ref.ptr) { ref.ptr = nullptr; }
5929 ~ufbx_unique_ptr() { traits::free(ptr); }
5930
5931 ufbx_unique_ptr &operator=(ufbx_unique_ptr &&ref) noexcept {
5932 if (&ref == this) return *this;
5933 ptr = ref.ptr;
5934 ref.ptr = nullptr;
5935 return *this;
5936 }
5937
5938 void reset(T *new_ptr=nullptr) noexcept {
5939 traits::free(ptr);
5940 ptr = new_ptr;
5941 }
5942
5943 void swap(ufbx_unique_ptr &ref) noexcept {
5944 T *tmp = ptr;
5945 ptr = ref.ptr;
5946 ref.ptr = tmp;
5947 }
5948
5949 T &operator*() const noexcept { return *ptr; }
5950 T *operator->() const noexcept { return ptr; }
5951 T *get() const noexcept { return ptr; }
5952 explicit operator bool() const noexcept { return ptr != nullptr; }
5953};

5955// Behaves like `std::shared_ptr<T>` except uses ufbx's internal reference counting,
5956// so it is half the size of a standard `shared_ptr` but might be marginally slower.
5957template <typename T>
5958class ufbx_shared_ptr {
5959 T *ptr;
5960 using traits = ufbx_type_traits<T>;
5961 static_assert(ufbx_type_traits<T>::valid, "ufbx_shared_ptr unsupported for type");
5962public:
5963
5964 ufbx_shared_ptr() noexcept : ptr(nullptr) { }
5965 explicit ufbx_shared_ptr(T *ptr_) noexcept : ptr(ptr_) { }
5966 ufbx_shared_ptr(const ufbx_shared_ptr &ref) noexcept : ptr(ref.ptr) { traits::retain(ref.ptr); }
5967 ufbx_shared_ptr(ufbx_shared_ptr &&ref) noexcept : ptr(ref.ptr) { ref.ptr = nullptr; }
5968 ~ufbx_shared_ptr() { traits::free(ptr); }
5969
5970 ufbx_shared_ptr &operator=(const ufbx_shared_ptr &ref) noexcept {
5971 if (&ref == this) return *this;
5972 traits::free(ptr);
5973 traits::retain(ref.ptr);
5974 ptr = ref.ptr;
5975 return *this;
5976 }
5977
5978 ufbx_shared_ptr &operator=(ufbx_shared_ptr &&ref) noexcept {
5979 if (&ref == this) return *this;
5980 ptr = ref.ptr;
5981 ref.ptr = nullptr;
5982 return *this;
5983 }
5984
5985 void reset(T *new_ptr=nullptr) noexcept {
5986 traits::free(ptr);
5987 ptr = new_ptr;
5988 }
5989
5990 void swap(ufbx_shared_ptr &ref) noexcept {
5991 T *tmp = ptr;
5992 ptr = ref.ptr;
5993 ref.ptr = tmp;
5994 }
5995
5996 T &operator*() const noexcept { return *ptr; }
5997 T *operator->() const noexcept { return ptr; }
5998 T *get() const noexcept { return ptr; }
5999 explicit operator bool() const noexcept { return ptr != nullptr; }
6000};
